precision_and_integration_comparison.conclusion: Neither the precision moment-root inverse nor increasing unchanged-core integration resolution from 120 to 480 removes the motor-off prefix heading divergence. The old inverse stopping rule and N=120 quadrature resolution are insufficient explanations by themselves for this local reproduction. A projection/representation or other common numerical-kernel effect remains to investigate; no unique cause is asserted.

quaternion_product_direct_check.method: Exact finite sums on deterministic weighted full-rank quaternion supports, direct Hamilton q_left*q_right vs core independent second-moment product.

findings: The algebraic 1/2 factor and sign in D are verified independently by a centered finite difference on a moderate deterministic matrix. Right action matrices commute with J, and their explicit equal-weight moment mixture matches the unchanged core target to roundoff.

Under full measured covariance, the first precision single-Bingham fit raises the global curvature bound from 50 to about 50.0077. All six pre-fit rotated components retain the bound to around 4e-14. The next gravity addition has D=0 and does not account for this increase.

Repeated moment projection amplifies the global operator bound rapidly (about 240.7 at tick2, 2646.6 at tick5, 136751 at tick20), while curvature at the fitted mode stays near 50 during these first20ticks. Global and modal-local curvature must not be interchanged.
Using the same precise inverse with integration480 retains this conclusion. The two isotropic covariance controls retain global curvature around or below50 during this tested interval.

The exact positive-mixture curvature identity certifies the yaw curvature bound for the unprojected recurrence. This finite counterexample identifies the single-Bingham projection stage as the first stage departing from that bound; it does not authorize a replacement probability model or closure.

standalone_first_projection_counterexamp.purpose: Bag-free fixed numerical input for independent reproduction of the first full-covariance gyro-mixture to single-Bingham projection and its global yaw-curvature bound increase.
standalone_first_projection_counterexamp.rotation_convention: R maps body to world; body-relative gyro quaternion increments multiply on the right; global world-z yaw multiplies on the left.
standalone_first_projection_counterexamp.cubature_order: covariance eigensystem columns in ascending-eigenvalue order; positive then negative sqrt(3) offset for each column
reproduction_steps: All requested arrays are numerical literals in this file; the original bag is unnecessary.
For each supplied delta quaternion form the supplied right-action matrix K. The exact six-component predicted density has components A_i=K_i A K_i.T with the equal weights above.
Verify that each component has the same maxeig(D) as input A, since K_i commutes with J.
Compute target M as mean(K_i M_input K_i.T), or use the supplied unchanged-core quaternion-product target. The two agree to roundoff.
Independently solve the same Bingham second-moment matching problem, using supplied precise fitted A as a result to check rather than as an observation input.

Evaluate maxeig(D) and q_mode.T D q_mode separately before/after moment projection and after adding next_acceleration_G. The first fit violates the global50bound while the local modal curvature remains approximately50.
standalone_first_projection_counterexamp.interpretation: The unprojected equal-weight component mixture preserves the input global bound. The fitted single Bingham violates it despite an accurate moment root. This is a fixed local projection counterexample; it does not authorize a different candidate family, moment target, noise law or product implementation.
